IMPLEMENTATION (two small changes in ConfluenceStorageRenderer.cs): HtmlEntityInlineRenderer, registered after LiteralInlineRenderer and well before the catch-all, writes Markdig's Transcoded value through the existing WriteEscaped; FlattenAltText gains 'case HtmlEntityInline' appending Transcoded, so an entity in image ALT TEXT stops throwing "no plain-text projection". DECISION FOR .claude/references/decisions.md (PENDING — the headless loop cannot write .claude/): ## 2026-07-24 — HTML entities: publish the resolved character, not the entity name A named or numeric character reference is published as the character it resolves to (Markdig's HtmlEntityInline.Transcoded), written back through WriteEscaped, rather than echoed as the source spelling. WHY: storage format is XML, and XML predefines only five entity names (amp, lt, gt, quot, apos). An HTML-only name such as © or   is UNDEFINED in an XML document, so echoing it invites Confluence to reject the body or silently rewrite it on save. A server-side rewrite is §8 content-hash drift, which invalidates an approval when nothing really changed (§9.2). Resolved characters are plain UTF-8 and unambiguous. This is the same reasoning as the strikethrough decision, which emits the editor's own rather than the shape that reads best in source. CONSEQUENCE: re-escaping keeps the round-trip honest. & transcodes to '&' and is written back as '&', never '&'. &/</> come out byte-identical; "/' resolve to a bare " and ', which need no escaping in element content and are re-escaped by WriteAttributeEscaped when the text lands in an attribute instead. CONSEQUENCE TO WATCH IN THE SANDBOX: page bodies now contain non-ASCII characters (©, —, →, …, U+00A0, astral codepoints). Confirm Confluence round-trips them byte-identically on save rather than re-encoding them as numeric character references. U+00A0 is the likeliest to be normalized by the editor. A re-encode would be §8 hash drift on any page containing a symbol. NOT DECIDED HERE: an unrecognized reference. Markdig never makes a node for '&nosuchthing;' or '©' with no semicolon — it leaves a LiteralInline, which already published correctly escaped, so no code was needed and none was written. PROBE FINDINGS (25 cases, tree + output per case; the method's 6th consecutive win, and used TWICE this slice — once before the fix to find the shape, once after to confirm all 25 rendered correctly before a single golden byte was written, which is why the golden matched first try): - Transcodings confirmed rather than assumed: ©/©/© -> U+00A9; ® U+00AE; ™ U+2122; — U+2014; → U+2192; … U+2026;   U+00A0; ' U+0027; " U+0022; 😀 -> SURROGATE PAIR U+D83D U+DE00, which WriteEscaped passes through intact because it writes chars consecutively to one writer. - ALREADY WORKING, NEEDED NOTHING: an entity in a LINK TITLE or a LINK URL (Markdig transcodes those into the string properties before the renderer sees them); an entity in a code span (never entity-parsed, so `©` -> ©); an entity in a FENCE (CDATA, survives verbatim); an unrecognized reference (stays LiteralInline). - THE ONE EXTRA BREAKAGE THE HANDOFF PREDICTED AND THE PROBE CONFIRMED: image alt text threw from FlattenAltText's default case, a different exception from a different call site, so '![a © b](p.png)' would still have failed if only the renderer had been added. DECISIONS PINNED BY TESTS: (1) Resolved character over source spelling (above). (2)   IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THE GOLDEN, and this is the slice's second real call. U+00A0 is invisible in a golden file, so a hand review (§4.3) could not tell it from a plain space, and a golden nobody can review by hand fails the rule's whole purpose. Pinned instead by Convert_resolves_nbsp_to_a_non_breaking_space, which spells the escape out explicitly in the C# literal. A dropped HTML comment inside entities.md (free since slice 12) records the omission and names the test, so the gap reads as deliberate rather than forgotten. DO NOT "complete" the golden by adding an   line. (3) THREE MORE FACTS A GOLDEN CANNOT EXPRESS: no double-escaping of &; '<script>' cannot smuggle live markup into the body (matters for §0.2, since Confluence content echoed back into a page is untrusted input); and '"' in image alt text is re-escaped by WriteAttributeEscaped so it cannot break out of the ac:alt attribute. WHAT WAS BUILT, in templates/workflows/docs-publish.yml: (1) a new "Answer the reviewers whose feedback shipped" step running `dotnet tool run docume sync --reply`, placed LAST BEFORE THE CARRY rather than immediately after the publish. THAT PLACEMENT IS THE DESIGN DECISION OF THE SLICE and it was a correction made mid-implementation: with the reply before the dashboard, a dashboard failure would skip the carry, lose the repliedAt stamps, and re-post every reply on the next publish — turning one answered comment into two. Every step between a posted reply and the commit that records it is such a failure, so the dashboard (which writes a Confluence page and nothing in the repo, so losing it costs a stale table until the next run) goes first. (2) The reply's EXIT CODE IS HELD — `code=0; dotnet tool run docume sync --reply || code=$?; echo "code=$code" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` — with a final step `if: steps.reply.outputs.code != '0'` turning it into a red check AFTER the carry. Reason: --reply stamps repliedAt per item the moment that item's reply lands (FeedbackInbox.MarkReplied, deliberately not batched), so a run that posts six of ten replies and then hits a 403 has six stamps on disk that must reach the repo — and the state file the publish just wrote holds the pageId of every page created in that run. Letting the step fail skips the carry and throws away both, so the six replies get posted again AND the next publish creates a second copy of every new page. (3) The paths step now also emits `inbox` and `archive` outputs, and the carry step (renamed "Carry the state file and the answered feedback into the docs/sync PR") copies both aside, restores both after the branch switch, and `git add "$state" "$inbox" "$archive"`. (4) The early-exit guard widened from `git diff --quiet -- "$state"` to `[ -z "$(git status --porcelain -- "$state" "$inbox" "$archive")" ]`. (5) The branch switch became `git checkout -f -B`. TWO MEASUREMENTS DROVE (4) AND (5) rather than reasoning: a reply-only run stamps items and leaves state.json BYTE-IDENTICAL (the reply half never sets `changed`, so SyncCommand skips StateStore.Save), so the old guard really would have exited early and dropped the stamps; and an UNFORCED switch to a docs/sync branch that already holds these files ABORTS, because unlike docs-sync.yml (where inbox items are new and untracked, so `git clean` clears them) these are tracked and `--reply` edits them in place, which `git clean` does not touch. docs-sync.yml was deliberately NOT changed: it never replies, so it has no stamps and no archive to carry. move-reorder-api.settledFrom: Atlassian's own REST docs (v1 api-group-content---children-and-descendants), the 2020-03-27 developer-community announcement, and Atlassian support's move/copy page doc. No live call — no sandbox space exists yet.

answers.a-exists-on-cloud: YES. Documented under v1 "Content — children and descendants", shipped 2020-03-27, NOT marked deprecated or experimental. Scopes: write:confluence-content (classic) / write:page:confluence (granular) — the same scope the publish already uses. 200 answers {"pageId": "<id>"}; documented errors are 400, 403, 404. v2 has NO move verb at all, so this is the only endpoint for it.
answers.b-does-it-spend-a-page-version: NO (docs + structure; not live-verified). The endpoint takes NO request body and therefore no version number, so unlike every other write it sits outside Confluence's optimistic-lock contract — there is no version to send and none comes back. Atlassian's support doc for move states a moved page keeps its full page history. THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERED: a reorder/move cannot silently revoke approval. Belt-and-braces anyway, because DocuMe keys invalidation off contentHash, which is body-only (§9.2) — even a version bump could not revoke approval here. DEFENSIVE DESIGN ADOPTED: never assume a moved page's version; the update path already re-reads remote version before every write (PublishExecutor.cs:312), so a stale Version in state costs nothing. Confirm on the first sandbox run.
answers.c-can-append-reparent: YES, and it is the cheaper move. `append` = "move the page to be a child of the target", so one bodyless PUT reparents. The v2 alternative (PUT /pages/{id} with a new parentId) works — DocuMe already sends parentId there, ConfluenceRequests.cs:36 — but requires the body and version.number, spending a page version for a change that touched no content. Use v1 move for a parent-only change; keep the v2 parentId for the case where the body is being rewritten anyway.
answers.d-stale-or-missing-target: 404, and it does NOT discriminate: page-gone and target-gone arrive identically. Handled by naming both ids in the operation string so the caller can tell a re-plan (target moved) from a recreate (page vanished). 403 is a permission refusal (moving needs edit on both pages) and stops the run per rule §1.2.

move-reorder-api.designImpact: One verb covers BOTH remaining M2 items: `append` is the §6.2 page move, `before`/`after` are the child-page ordering post-pass PLAN.md §6.2 line 246 asks for ("reconcile each parent's child order ... using minimal move operations; disable with --no-reorder"). Atlassian's own caution is load-bearing and is documented on ConfluencePageMovePosition: NEVER use before/after when the target is a top-level page — it moves the page to the space top level where it does not appear in the page tree. DocuMe's tree always hangs under confluence.rootPageId (§5.1), so a reorder reorders children of a known parent; the client cannot enforce this (it would need a read) so the caller owns it.

label-author.question: PLAN.md §13 S3: label add/remove endpoint (v1 content/{id}/label) behavior on Cloud, and can we get WHO added a label?
label-author.answer: NO — Confluence Cloud exposes no label author anywhere DocuMe can reach. CQL search results (`rest/api/content/search`) carry the page, not the labelling event; v1 `GET content/{id}/label` answers {prefix,name,id,label} with no creator and no timestamp; v2 `/pages/{id}/labels` is the same four fields. The audit-log API that would know is admin-scoped and not something a docs tool should require. NOT live-verified (no sandbox space yet), but three independent documented shapes agreeing is enough to stop looking.
label-author.resolution: Took §6.3's own documented fallback: approvedBy is the literal "unknown" (LabelSyncPlanner.UnknownApprover), and approval still works because the label — not the name — is the gesture §8 keys on. THE RULE THAT MATTERS: never fill it from the account DocuMe authenticates as. The reviewer and the bot are different people, and a fabricated approver in a financial org's audit trail (§8 line 305) is worse than an honest unknown. The add/remove half of S3 was already settled in M2: AddLabelsAsync/RemoveLabelAsync work and are WireMock-tested, with `?name=` chosen over the path-segment form so a configurable label containing a slash stays representable.
